title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. f: X -> S is smooth, with p nilpotent on S (in practice S of characteristic p, where p-curvature is a linear object). The page studies three Picard-type functors of line bundles with integrable connection: Pic^{ci} (all integrable connections, i.e. Pic^natural), Pic^{cip} (p-curvature zero) and Pic^{cin} (nilpotent p-curvature). The aim is to describe the 'crystalline Picard functor' P^{cris}, which the next page treats. By Berthelot/Katz, a module with integrable connection is a crystal exactly when its p-curvature is (quasi-)nilpotent, so Pic^{cin} is the crystalline Picard functor.

(i) p-curvature as a homomorphism. For a line bundle the p-curvature psi(nabla) is a horizontal p-linear form, i.e. a section of the Frobenius-twisted 1-forms Omega^1_{X'/S} = Omega^{(p)}. On tensor products of line bundles psi is additive. This gives a group homomorphism Pic^{ci}_{X/S} -> f_*(Omega^{(p)}_{X/S}).
- Its kernel is Pic^{cip}. By Cartier descent, Pic^{cip} is essentially the Picard functor of the Frobenius twist X^{(p/S)}, hence 'bien compris'.
- This gives (4.1): 0 -> Pic^{cip} -> Pic^{ci} -> f_*(Omega^{(p)}) / overline{f_*(Omega^{(p)})}.
- Here the overline denotes the formal completion of the vector group along its zero section, i.e. the subsheaf of nilpotent sections (the 'groupe formel').

(ii) Pic^{cin} is the inverse image of that formal subgroup. Hence (4.2)/(4.3): 0 -> Pic^{cip} -> Pic^{cin} -> overline{f_*(Omega^{(p)})}. So the crystalline Picard functor is an extension of a subgroup of a formal vector group by the Frobenius-twisted Picard functor. The page identifies Pic^{cin} with Pic^{0 p/S}-type objects (the transcription's 'Ric').

(iii) Kernel of forgetting the connection. Grothendieck then studies V = Ker(Pic^{cin} -> Pic_{X/S}), i.e. connections on the trivial bundle (4.4).
- Integrable connections d + omega on O_X are closed 1-forms, modulo dlog of units: f_*Z^1 / dlog f_*(O_X^*).
- The p-curvature of d + omega is (up to Frobenius twist) omega' - C(omega), by Katz's formula, where C is the Cartier operator.
- Hence the dévissage (4.5): 0 -> Cart_{X/S} -> V -> overline{f_*(Omega^{(p)})}. Cart is the 'Cartier sheaf' of closed forms with C(omega) = omega, modulo logarithmic differentials. By Cartier's theorem (exactness of 0 -> O^* -F-> O^* -dlog-> Z^1 -(1-C)-> Omega^1 -> 0 in the étale/flat topology), this is essentially a piece of R^1 f_* mu_p.

(iv) Next page. For Pic^0 an abelian scheme, Pic^{cris,0} is the formal completion of the universal vector extension E (= Pic^natural) along the Frobenius-twisted abelian scheme B^{(p/S)} sitting inside E. This is finer information than the formal group hat-E at the origin.

This is the circle of ideas of Grothendieck's 1970 'cristaux et groupes de Barsotti-Tate' programme, worked out by Mazur-Messing.
errors: When p is only nilpotent on S (not zero), p-curvature is not directly a linear section of f_*Omega^{(p)}. The maps in (4.1)-(4.4) make literal sense only for S of characteristic p, or after reduction. Grothendieck seems aware of this, since the previous page defines nilpotence via values on reduced S'.
(4.1)-(4.4) are only left exact; no surjectivity onto the formal subgroup is claimed or proved.

The identification of Pic^{cin} with a (Frobenius-twisted) Pic^0-type object written under (4.3) is unexplained and, as written, cannot hold in general without hypotheses (e.g. Pic^0 an abelian scheme, V-divisibility, which is assumed only on the next page).

In (4.4) V should be the kernel of Pic^{cin} -> Pic (connections on the trivial bundle with nilpotent p-curvature). The displayed quotient f_*Z^1/Im dlog f_*O^* is V for Pic^{ci}, not Pic^{cin}, so the target should be read accordingly.

ideas.what: p-curvature as a homomorphism Pic^natural -> f_*Omega^1_{X'/S} with kernel the line bundles with p-curvature zero (Cartier descent to X')
ideas.modern_name: p-curvature map on Pic^natural; Pic(X') -> Pic^natural(X) -> H^0(X',Omega^1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz (1970, Nilpotent connections and the monodromy theorem); Mazur-Messing (1974); used later by Bezrukavnikov-Braverman, Ogus-Vologodsky
ideas.where_published: unsure; ideas around Grothendieck's 1970 Nice/Montréal 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux'

ideas.what: Crystalline Picard functor as line bundles with integrable connection of nilpotent p-curvature: extension of a formal subgroup of a vector group by Pic of the Frobenius twist
ideas.modern_name: crystalline Picard / Pic of crystals; nilpotent-p-curvature locus = formal completion

ideas.what: Dévissage of connections on the trivial bundle: closed forms mod dlog, with kernel of p-curvature the Cartier-fixed forms mod dlog (the 'Cartier sheaf')
ideas.modern_name: Cartier operator; Z^1 with C=1 equals dlog O^*; relation to R^1 f_* mu_p

ideas.what: Pic^{cris,0} as formal completion of the universal vector extension along the Frobenius-twisted abelian scheme (next page)
ideas.modern_name: crystalline nature of the universal extension E(A^*)

missed.claim: The page gives an explicit three-step dévissage of the crystalline Picard functor: Cart (Cartier-fixed forms mod dlog) -> V -> formal vector group, then Pic^{cip} = Pic of the Frobenius twist, then formal completion of H^0(Omega'). This is a working sketch rather than a new result; essentially equivalent statements appear in Mazur-Messing and later p-curvature literature.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor historical interest: it documents Grothendieck's own route to Mazur-Messing-type results via p-curvature and the Cartier operator, a route that connects to modern rank-one nonabelian Hodge theory in characteristic p.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is coherent but standard: the p-curvature homomorphism on Pic^natural, Cartier descent, nilpotent p-curvature as crystals, and the Cartier operator dévissage are all in Katz, Berthelot and Mazur-Messing. It is a draft-level sketch with no evident uncredited result.
transcription_corrections: 'Ric' is almost certainly 'Pic' (underlined Pic, e.g. Pic^{0 p/S}_{X/S}).
'moyen' (arrow label in (4.4) and 'c'est le moyen de') should read 'noyau': V is the kernel of Pic^{cin}_{X/S} -> Pic_{X/S}.
'Omega^{⊗p}' is more plausibly Omega^{(p)} (the Frobenius-twisted Omega^1_{X/S}), the natural target of p-curvature.
Line before (4.4): 'étudier le noyau V de Pic^{cin}_{X/S} -> Pic_{X/S}'.
Line 4: 'Mod. inversibles sur X/S muni d'une connexion ... à connexion compatible aux puissances p-ièmes'.
